newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung Elec to absorb Kwangju Elec.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Elec to absorb Kwangju Elec.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co Ltd said on Monday it had agreed to absorb its unlisted Kwangju Electronics Co unit as of July 1, 1997.
Following the announcement the Korea Stock Exchange said it was suspending trading in shares of Samsung Electronics. Trading in the stock will resume on Tuesday.
Samsung, which currently holds 95 percent of Kwangju Electronics, plans to hold a shareholders' meeting on February 28 for a formal approval of the merger, a Samsung spokesman said.
"We have decided to absorb Kwangju Electronics to reduce inefficiency and avoid overlapping investment in home appliances," the spokesman said.

Samsung has said that it will buy shares from shareholders opposing the merger for 20 days after the meeting, a statement from the Security Supervisory Board said. It will pay 64,330 won per common share and 31,711 won per preferred share.
Samsung common stocks closed the morning trade at 60,100 won, down 200, while its preferred shares ended at 29,900, down 600. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5643
